python.code:
import thinkthen as tt

ask = "Does the customer ask for a refund?"

# a plain ask for money back: True
print(tt.decide(ask,
    "Please refund my order. It arrived broken."))

# build a question once. The band's middle is "not sure"
refund = tt.question(decide=ask, threshold=(0.2, 0.8))

# an exchange, or money back? not sure: None
print(tt.decide(refund,
    "I want to send this back."))

# a list goes in, and one filled form per report comes out
reports = ["CSV export fails. Steps: click Export.",
    "The login page spins and nobody can sign in.",
    "The Pay button on the billing page is too blue."]
for form in tt.annotate("form.json", reports):
    print(form)

printed.see: Each form fills steps, area, and impact.

ruby.code:
require "thinkthen"

# the one line that gives the refund deadline
policy = ["Returns need the original receipt.",
    "Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.",
    "Shipping is free on orders over $50."]
ask = "Which line gives the refund deadline?"
puts ThinkThen.find(ask, policy).unit

# praise, a bug, and a double charge in one message
labels = ["praise", "bug", "billing"]
p ThinkThen.tag("Which labels fit this message?",
    "Love it, but export crashes and I was billed twice.",
    labels:)

Refunds are issued within 30 days of purchase.
["praise", "bug", "billing"]

library(thinkthen)
body <- c("I was billed twice for one order.",
  "My parcel is a week late.",
  "I am locked out of my account.")
teams <- c("billing", "shipping", "account")
# each ticket goes to the team its words name
data.frame(body, team = tt_choose("Which team owns this?",
  body, teams))
# only the double bill is about money, so it ranks first
tt_rank("Is this about money?", body, top = 1)
